prs.head: efee7e7c8a2fda0608cdc2f311f2b2fd5a87355e
prs.author: MikaMcFlurry
prs.body:
Owner decision (2026-10-09, follow-up to PR #18): from now on the Verlauf should show whether a play came from the cassette or was a recommendation. Because nothing read-only can establish that afterwards, this PR records it when the play is recorded. This is the separately reviewed storage scope that PR #18 left open.

## Change
- **Additive migration 5:** `ALTER TABLE plays ADD COLUMN lane TEXT`. No other schema change, no data rewrite; existing rows keep `NULL`.
- **Stamped once, at record time:** in `recordPlays` (Spotify's recently-played list) and `recordSeenPlay` (plays counted from looks). It is set only when all three hold:
  1. the play's context is the station's own playlist (`deckUri`);
  2. the deck in that playlist was written before the song began (`deck.writtenAt <= start`);
  3. the deck holds the song for exactly one reason.
- Anything else stays `NULL`. The native guest-sample insert also stays `NULL`.
- **Read-only display:** `history()` reads the stamp. Nothing recomputes it, so a new mix, a later recommendation or a guest replay never changes an old row.
- **UI:** the existing two-question tags. The Verlauf header says sources appear for new plays from your cassettes.
- Scheduling, the planner, guest decisions, memory and session logic are unchanged. The only write change is one more column in the two existing INSERTs.

## Tests
- Real Hub/FakeSpotify playback stamps each station play with its deck reason. History returns exactly the stored stamp.
- Owner play → kept recommendation → guest mode with a new queue and 20 min replay → guest off → new queue 25 h later: every owner row's source and `ignored: false` stay as stamped.
- Each doubt case gives `null`: no context, another playlist, a deck written after the song began, a song held twice for two reasons.
- Migrating a version-4 store adds the column, keeps every play row unchanged, and history shows no source for them.
- Reading the Verlauf leaves `plays`, `memory`, `stations`, `discoveries` and `kv` unchanged.
- The legacy migration fixtures in `recovery.test.ts` and `session.test.ts` reset a store to version 3. They now also drop `lane`, since a real version-3 store wouldn't have it. Their assertions are unchanged and pass.

## Checks
- typecheck and lint: clean (2 infos)
- unit/Worker: 488/488 with `--testTimeout=120000`
- browser: 41/41
- build and `wrangler deploy --dry-run`: OK

Not run: live Spotify, physical iPhone, HA/MA, populated-storage restore. The migration runs on the first wake of each account's Durable Object after deploy.

This answers the review of `2b3abfd`. **PR20-LANE-01 is fixed.** The new head is `d716055`.

**What changed**
- `laneOf` (start estimated as stamp minus length) is removed.
- The lane is now noted from a look that sees the song **arrive**. In `sync`, `noteLane` creates a note when all of these hold:
  - the player shows a song in a station's own playlist;
  - the stored look before showed a different song or context;
  - the deck in that playlist was written before that earlier look.
- The note freezes the deck's single reason for the song, or `null` if the deck holds it for several.
- When the play is recorded (`recordPlays` / `recordSeenPlay`, context = the station's playlist), `laneFor` takes the newest note for that song and station from before the play's stamp. The note is used once.
- Without a note the lane stays `null`.
- Pauses, restarts or a new deck before the listing don't change a note. Nothing is relabelled afterwards, and already stored history and counters stay untouched.
- Notes expire after 2 days, and at most 50 are kept in kv `lane_notes`.

**Regression (real Hub/FakeSpotify; the replacement deck is a controlled SQL fixture, as in your reproduction)**
- The song begins with lane X and is paused 30 s in.
- 30 min later a new deck holds the same song as Y, with `writtenAt = now`; the hub restarts.
- Another 30 min later the song resumes, plays 150 s until it is listed, then a forced sync.
- Result: history is X or `null`, never Y.
- On `2b3abfd` this test fails with `'favorite'`, matching your result.

**Also covered**
- The first song after a start is not seen arriving by any earlier look, so it gets `null`.
- Real playback stamps either the deck's single reason or `null`.
- The migration test and the read-only test still pass.
- Same song ID in several decks or sources: a note is only made when this deck holds the song for exactly one reason.
- Unknown or foreign context, or songs inserted from outside or natively: no note, so `null`.
- Guest and private plays: their `ignored` handling is unchanged.

prs.author: MikaMcFlurry
prs.body:
Owner request (2026-10-09): a fixed device, e.g. in a party room, whose music never counts. true-shuffle should switch guest mode on by itself while that device plays.

## How it works
**Setting**
- Stored in kv `guest_devices` as `{id, name}`, at most 20 entries.
- Set with `PUT /api/guest/devices` (session and CSRF like the other routes).
- Returned as `AppState.guest.devices`. No schema change.

**Behaviour**
- On every look at the player (`sync`, before `noteGuestLast`):
  - **Guest device seen playing:** guest time opens from the start of its current song, or is held open for 15 min past the look. Looks come at least every 10 min while something plays.
  - **Another device or nothing playing:** guest time ends there with `tail: null`, so the song then playing is not treated as the guest's.
- A device matches by id or, when Spotify gives it a new id, by name.
- **Guest time switched on by hand is never touched.** Switching on by hand while a device period is open turns it into a hand-made period.
- **Everything else is the existing guest logic:** plays inside guest time are stored ignored, never reach memory, and show "Gast" in the Verlauf.
- **Known limit, stated in the UI:** true-shuffle only knows what its looks see.
  - Looks happen about every minute with the app open and about every ten minutes otherwise.
  - A song that started and ended on the device between two looks can still count.

**UI**
- Geräte has a new section "Immer im Gast-Modus" with one switch per device: the saved ones plus those Spotify shows right now.
- Jetzt and Mehr name the device while it holds guest mode on, e.g. „Partyraum“ spielt, das zählt nicht.

## Tests
- Real Hub/FakeSpotify, phone → party room → phone:
  - all party-room plays are stored ignored and memory for those songs is unchanged;
  - `state.guest` reads `{ active: true, device: "Partyraum" }`;

prs.body:
Owner request (2026-10-09): a recap like Spotify's yearly one, but always available and more detailed. It covers genres, listening times, how long and how much the owner listens, and what true-shuffle learns about them, with charts.

## Data (no change to counting, scheduling or playback)
- **`GET /api/profile?tz=<IANA>`**: read-only, built from the plays log.
  - Covers 180 days; guest time is left out. Hours are bucketed in the listener's zone.
  - Returns:
    - plays, hours (song lengths added up, labelled as an upper estimate) and distinct songs/artists
    - plays by weekday × hour
    - months
    - top 10 artists and top 10 songs
    - the share played on cassettes
  - It also returns what true-shuffle keeps about the listener: favourites, songs never to play again, recommendations kept or dropped, and early skips.
  - It writes nothing and makes no Spotify request.
- **Imported history summary**
  - During import, the browser builds a compact summary from the export files: real `ms_played`, hours, months, and the top 50 artists and songs. The files never leave the device.
  - It is sent once with `POST /api/history/profile`. The server checks every number and name length and stores it in kv `history_profile`, replacing the previous one.
  - The per-track counting from the import is unchanged.
- **`POST /api/profile/genres`**
  - The configured AI estimates the genre mix and writes a two-sentence description. The AI is Claude via the existing `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` and SDK call pattern, otherwise Workers AI.
  - Input is the top 50 artists, weighted by listening time.
  - At most one estimate every six hours. It is stored in kv `genre_estimate` and shown as "Einschätzung der KI", with its source and date.
  - Spotify's genre data is not used, because it would cost requests from the shared quota.
  - A refusal or an unusable reply keeps the previous estimate.

## Page `/profil`
- Linked from the Verlauf header, from Mehr, and from the end of an import.
- A switch chooses between "Ganzer Verlauf" (the import) and "Letzte 180 Tage" (live data).
- **Charts:**
  - hours as the hero figure, with three smaller figures
  - a weekday × hour grid in one data colour, stepped light to dark, with hover titles and an "Als Tabelle" view
  - columns per month, switching to per year past 24 months; only the busiest column is labelled
  - top artists as bars with the value at the tip
  - top songs with covers where the library knows them
- **Text sections:** genres (AI estimate) and "Was true-shuffle über dich weiß".
- No overflow at 320, 390 or 1280 px in light and dark. The number labels on bars and columns stay inside.

## Tests
- **Live profile**
  - It counts only the owner's plays, and the weekday × hour grid matches each play's Berlin weekday and hour.
  - Months and grid add up to the play count.
  - It writes nothing to `plays`, `memory`, `stations`, `discoveries` or `kv`.
  - An unknown zone falls back to UTC, and plays older than 180 days are left out.
- **Import summary**
  - Only plays of 30 s or more count; real listening time, the early-skip count, top lists and size bounds are checked.
  - The server refuses malformed summaries.
- **Genres:** weighted artist shares go into the prompt; the shares come back scaled to 100; repeat requests are throttled to one per six hours; no AI and no listening are handled; the reply parser is tested.
- **Browser:** import a generated history file, open the Hörprofil, see "Ganzer Verlauf" with hours, Nachtbus among the artists and the month chart, then switch to "Letzte 180 Tage".

## Checks
- typecheck and lint: clean (2 infos)
- unit/Worker: 497/497 with `--testTimeout=120000`
- browser: 42/42
- build and `wrangler deploy --dry-run`: OK

Not run: a real import of the owner's export, a live AI call (unit tests use a stub runner), physical iPhone.

Alle fünf Befunde aus dem letzten Review sind in `fd26744` behoben:

- **PR22-AI-01** (KI-Aufruf hält das Konto-Lock): `requestGenres` bereitet unter dem Lock vor, ruft die KI **außerhalb** des Locks auf und speichert danach wieder unter dem Lock. Der Anthropic-Aufruf ist auf 20 s begrenzt und läuft ohne Retries, Workers AI hängt an `withTimeout`. Gleichzeitige Anfragen teilen sich einen Flug. Test `test/worker/genre-userhub.test.ts` lädt die echten UserHub-Methoden: Pause geht durch, während die KI blockiert ist.
- **PR22-AI-02** (Sperre nur nach Erfolg): Jeder Versuch wird vor dem Aufruf dauerhaft gespeichert (`genre_attempt {at,id}`). Die 6-Stunden-Sperre gilt deshalb auch nach Fehlern und Neustarts. Ein neuer Import macht eine noch offene Antwort ungültig. Die Oberfläche zeigt „wieder ab …“ und meldet unbrauchbare Antworten ehrlich.
- **PR22-IMPORT-RECENT**: Ein Export, der nur Plays nach der ersten Anmeldung enthält, wird nicht mehr abgewiesen. Gespeichert wird dann nur das Hörprofil, ohne `/api/history/import`. Ein früherer Memory-Import bleibt dabei unverändert, die Grenze gegen Doppelzählung bleibt bestehen. Neuer e2e-Test.
- **PR22-IMPORT-SILENT**: Schlägt das Speichern des Profils fehl, gibt es einen Teilstatus: Die Zählungen sind übernommen, das Hörprofil nicht. Der Button „Hörprofil erneut speichern“ sendet nur das Profil. Der e2e-Test (503 auf `/api/history/profile`) belegt, dass dabei genau ein Import-Request entsteht.
- **PR22-CHART-A11Y**: „Als Tabelle“ zeigt jetzt alle 168 Werte (24 Stunden × 7 Tage, mit Tagessummen) und jeden Monat bzw. jedes Jahr mit Stunden und Songs. Die Tabellen haben eine Caption und lassen sich per Tastatur fokussieren und scrollen. Geprüft bei 320 und 390 px in hell und dunkel ohne Seitenüberlauf. Bei 320 px scrollt die Wochentabelle innerhalb ihres Kastens, die Stundenspalte bleibt dabei stehen.

Beide neuen Import-Tests schlagen mit dem alten Code fehl. Lokal laufen typecheck, lint, 499 Unit-/Worker-Tests, 44 Browsertests, Build und `wrangler deploy --dry-run` grün.
